title: unify-go-stream-connector-auth-and-idempotent-reconnect-v1.0.0
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Go SDK 1.0.0: introduce StreamConnector API with unified auth provider and idempotent reconnect semantics; connection pooling for high-throughput consumers; ergonomic guards for context cancellation and backoff tuning. Migration guide included.
description:
Context and motivation: Different SDKs (Go/TS/Py) had subtle behavioral drift around streaming auth refresh and reconnect semantics which caused hard-to-debug partial-resume failures in multi-tenant environments. This PR consolidates the Go SDK's streaming surface around a new StreamConnector abstraction, aligns the token lifecycle hooks with the cross-sdk auth contract, and implements an idempotent reconnect state machine so consumers see deterministic resume/failure semantics. This work is part of ENG-4021 and coordinates with parallel updates in the TS and Python SDKs (follow-ups tracked).

What this PR does (single string description): - Add StreamConnector interface (Connect/Recv/Close/OnReauth) that decouples transport from token lifecycle - Implement IdempotentReconnect state machine that guarantees at-most-once reconnection attempts per logical cursor and provides an explicit ReconnectBackoff policy - Introduce PluggableTokenProvider with synchronous/async reauth hooks and a defensive token cache with TTL jitter - Add a small connection pool used by high-throughput clients to amortize handshake cost while preserving per-call auth scoping - Normalize retry policy to exponential backoff with capped jitter and an opt-in aggressive-reconnect mode for low-latency consumers - Improve context propagation and cancellation handling so canceling parent contexts cleanly closes streams without leaking goroutines - Add unit and integration tests covering token rotation during in-flight streams, reconnect races, and pool churn - Bump go module to v1.0.0 and publish changelog + migration notes.

Checklist (what was completed): - [x] Design and RFC (ENG-4021) approved - [x] Implementation of StreamConnector and token provider - [x] Idempotent reconnect and backoff policy - [x] Connection pool with configurable size and metrics hooks - [x] End-to-end integration tests against local test harness - [x] Benchmark microbench for high-FPS streaming with pool enabled - [x] Docs: migration guide and examples

Commits (summary): - feat(stream): add StreamConnector interface and default implementation - feat(auth): pluggable token provider + TTL cache and reauth hook - perf(pool): add connection pool and bench harness - fix(stream): race fixes for reconnect FSM - test: add integration tests for token rotation and pool eviction - docs: migration guide and changelog - chore: bump go mod to v1.0.0

Files changed (high level): - sdk/go/stream/connector.go (new) - sdk/go/stream/reconnect_fsm.go (new) - sdk/go/auth/token_provider.go (modified/expanded) - sdk/go/pool/conn_pool.go (new) - sdk/go/internal/metrics/stream_metrics.go (modified) - examples/streams/reconnect_example.go (new) - docs/migration/go-1.0.0-streaming.md (new) - go.mod, go.sum

Review conversation (high-level excerpts): - Ethan: "Can you clarify failure semantics if a reauth fails while there are pending messages in flight? We need to ensure consumers see a single terminal error or resume, not both." — Maya: "Implemented ReauthResult with explicit terminal vs transient error categories and added tests that assert only one terminal callback is delivered per logical cursor." - Priya: "Pooling is great, but we should fail fast on exhausted pools when aggressive mode is off." — Maya: "Added immediate-fail behavior when pool is exhausted and consumer opted out of waiting; documented opt-in behavior." - Samir: "Please add an integration test for delayed token rotation under high throughput." — Maya: "Added test that rotates tokens mid-stream and asserts no duplicated messages and correct resume cursor." - QA: noted intermittent integration flakes on CI related to external harness; reran integration suite and all passed.

CI and checks: - go build: pass - unit tests: pass (coverage: 82%) - integration tests: initially flaky, re-run: pass - linters (golangci-lint): pass - benchmarks: microbench recorded ~18% lower p99 latency for pooled consumers vs baseline. CI annotated with links to artifacts.

Migration notes (consumer-facing summary): - New StreamConnector is backwards-compatible with existing stream client via an adapter; most consumers can enable the new behavior by setting ClientConfig.StreamConnector = stream.DefaultConnector() - If you relied on automatic unbounded reconnects with no backoff, you must opt-in to aggressive reconnect mode to preserve that pattern - If you implement a custom token provider, implement OnReauth(ctx) -> (newToken, err) and honor token TTL; see docs/migration/go-1.0.0-streaming.md for examples.

Follow-ups / coordination: - TS and Python SDK teams to merge parity adapters (ENG-4088) and confirm identical observable metrics and retry defaults - Add telemetry tag for reconnect.reason to help surface production incidents - Add a canary rollout to Dedicated (small subset of customers) before platform-wide rollout - Publish blog note on best practices for streaming auth and pooling (tracking ENG-4122)

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main on 2026-02-25 by Maya Patel. Commit message: "feat(go): StreamConnector + idempotent reconnect + token provider; bump v1.0.0". Tag created: v1.0.0-go. Release artifacts: changelog and migration doc attached to release draft.

Notes: This PR was intentionally conservative about changing public function signatures — primary surface change is the client config opt-in. The goal was to fix observed nondeterministic reconnects and auth races while keeping migration friction minimal. The Go implementation includes a stress-tested FSM and comprehensive tests; subsequent PRs will port small ergonomic helpers into TS/Py to complete parity.
